deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. Folio 165 is prose notes in German on Hellenistic (Seleucid) history. It continues seamlessly from the previous page (Antiochus IV Epiphanes, Antiochus V Eupator) and runs into the next page (Demetrius II Nicator, Tryphon, Cleopatra Thea). The style looks like notes taken from a lecture or textbook on ancient history (Göttingen-style universal history, e.g. Heeren); I do not recognise the hand as Gauss's own working hand. The page number 165 is pencilled in a later archival hand.

Content, item by item (dates BC):
1. Antiochus V Eupator stands under his guardian Philip. Philip quarrels with Lysias and is killed in 162.
2. The Romans exploit the situation. The phrase is probably 'u. richteten d. Kriegsmacht zu Grunde', i.e. they destroyed the Seleucid fleet and elephants (embassy of Cn. Octavius).
3. Mithridates (I), king of Parthia, makes conquests in the East.
4. Demetrius, a hostage in Rome, petitions for leave to return. Refused, he flees, reaches Syria and becomes king as Demetrius I Soter, 161–150.
5. Heraclides, expelled from Babylon by Demetrius, wins Alexander Balas to his cause. He passes Balas off as a son of Epiphanes and presents him in Rome to obtain the kingdom.
6. The princes of Asia Minor are to set Balas on the throne. After two battles the war ends in Demetrius' downfall, and Balas becomes king in 150.
7. Balas marries Cleopatra (Thea), daughter of Ptolemy VI Philometor. He sinks into debauchery and leaves the government to a certain Ammonius.

Nothing is computed, so no mathematical problem is served.
errors: Historical slip: Demetrius I is usually dated as arriving and seizing power in 162 BC, not 161 (though some chronologies give 161).
Historical slip: Antiochus V Eupator's reign is usually given as 164–162, not 164–161 (previous page).
Historical simplification: Heraclides was a finance official/governor associated with Babylon (his brother Timarchus was the satrap). Calling him 'Satrap von Babylon' conflates the two.
No mathematical errors to report; the page contains no mathematics.

results.what: Lecture/reading notes on Seleucid dynastic history (Antiochus V, Demetrius I Soter, Alexander Balas), c. 164–150 BC
results.modern_name: Ancient history (Hellenistic Seleucid kingdom); not mathematics
results.usually_credited_to: Standard historiography (Polybius, Josephus, 1 Maccabees; 18th/19th-century textbooks such as Heeren)

deep.surprise_reason: These are non-mathematical history notes of routine textbook content. They are possibly not even in Gauss's hand and may be student or lecture notes bound into the bundle. There is nothing of mathematical-historical significance.
transcription_corrections: Line 3–4: 'u. verstatteten[?] d. Kriegsmacht zu ...[?]' is more plausibly 'u. richteten d. Kriegsmacht zu Grunde'. This fits the Roman destruction of the Seleucid fleet and elephants in 162.
Line 7: 'da es diese aber nicht erhielt' should read 'da er diese aber nicht erhielt'.
Lines 6–7: the reading 'Erlaubniss ... zu reisen zu ...' is uncertain. The sense is permission to return home (e.g. 'zurück gehen zu dürfen'); the exact wording is illegible to me.
'Usurpateur', 'Heraclidas', 'Alexander Balas', 'Ammonius' and 'Mitridat' are confirmed from the image.
